page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized server instance designed for GPU-intensive workloads. It features two NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with a combined 80 GB of VRAM, paired with 24 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, containing 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2.0 threads per core) and dedicated CPU allocation. System memory totals 170.0 GB, providing approximately 7.08 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated operations. Single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, falling in the bottom 25% for stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations score in the average tier. Conversely, the server excels in LLM inference benchmarks, achieving top-tier results (top 10%) for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, as well as text generation for 7B and 70B parameter models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high-density GPU and memory allocation make this instance a specialized resource. While the lower single-core CPU performance represents a bottleneck for general-purpose compute tasks, the hardware profile is optimized to offset these limitations during parallel processing workloads. The a2-highgpu-2g is best suited for deep learning, large language model inference, data science pipelines, and parallel scientific computing where GPU acceleration is the primary driver of execution speed.
